Chile. A long, narrow country stretching along South America's western coast, bordered by the Andes to the east and the Pacific to the west. Its distinctive geography ranges from the hyperarid Atacama Desert in the north to temperate regions and fjords in the south. Home to diverse cultures from pre-Columbian societies to modern Latin American literature, Chile has become a crucial node in both geographic and intellectual discussions of the continent.

Chile is a ribbon-shaped nation extending over twenty-six hundred miles north to south but rarely more than one hundred ten miles wide, one of Earth's most extreme geographical proportions. The Atacama Desert occupies its northern territory and is the driest non-polar desert on Earth. Some regions have never recorded rainfall in recorded history. Chile borders the Andes Mountains along its entire eastern frontier, with peaks exceeding twenty thousand feet, creating some of the world's most dramatic topography. It contains Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui, far out in the Pacific, adding mystique and archaeological significance. The island's indigenous Rapa Nui people developed a unique megalithic culture.

Chile is a major copper producer and exporter, controlling significant global reserves. Mineral wealth drives both its economy and its geopolitical importance in South America. Politically democratic and economically developed by regional standards, Chile is a gateway to understanding modern Latin American political culture and stability. The Atacama spans over six hundred miles and creates a striking geographic boundary between radically different climatic zones, enabling unique ecosystems in the transition zones. Chile connects to the Atacama Desert which occupies its northern territory and is one of Earth's most inhospitable environments, to the Andes which form its eastern spine and geographical backbone, to South America as its southwesternmost major nation, to Peru as its northern neighbor and former rival for territorial claims, to Argentina with which it shares the Andes and a long border as a regional rival, and to the Pacific Ocean which shapes its western identity and trade routes.
